summary.prose: Building this fix teaches the workflow that a standalone feature's LLD heads its work item. The core change is one head reader in storage.ts that the task resolver and folder naming both use, followed by the resolver changes that let the build tool admit standalone plan tasks without disturbing epic or bugfix resolution. Alongside that, head artifacts get names from a written title, triage starts carrying the SPEC a feature came from, and the docs migrator learns to gather already-split standalone folders, which is then run once over this repo.

tasks.title: Make readEpicDefinitionCore the single work-item head reader
tasks.summary: In storage.ts: readArtifactCore also reads meta.tracker; EpicDefinitionCore gains headKind and tracker; readEpicDefinitionCore tries DEF, then ISSUE, then the lowest-ordinal LLD-<h>-<story>, reporting an LLD head with standalone: true and createdAt = epicCreatedAt ?? createdAt. All existing consumers (inheritedEpicSlug, inheritedStandalone, inheritedStoryStandalone, readEpicCreatedAt, buildRecordFolderArgs, validate resolveRouteFlag) then see LLD heads with no code change of their own.
acceptanceChecks: DEF beats ISSUE beats LLD; a lone LLD (flagged or unflagged) heads its hash with headKind 'LLD' and standalone: true; lowest-ordinal LLD wins; malformed LLD -> {}.
DEF/ISSUE heads keep their existing fields and now also carry tracker.
A legacy unflagged LLD-only item's BUILD/TESTS placement resolves to docs/standalone.
finalizePlan for an LLD-only standalone work item inherits the LLD's slug and writes PLAN.md into the LLD's folder.
